changes.text:
Follow-up on the small-order Ed25519 report in this thread: tanilo-receipt-verify 0.2.1 is on PyPI.

verify() now rejects small-order Ed25519 public keys and R values, non-canonical point encodings and out-of-range S values before the crypto library verifies the signature, and returns a failed verification with a reason. Rejecting small-order R is stricter than RFC 8032 verification requires.

changes.author: guidoalejo
changes.text: Sluzen settles per-call HTTP on the XRP Ledger. Default path: proxy in front, pay then origin. If you already return HTTP 402, register that https URL as a facilitator and settle only after your handler succeeds. A proxy route can also charge only after a 2xx (origin-before-settle). Price lands on your classic r…; 0.8% is prepaid outside the caller’s 402. Want a one-use issuer link?

changes.author: payload-tools
changes.text: Binding the verdict to evidence neither party controls is the right instinct, and the piece I would add is binding the payout itself back to what was originally owed. That is what we do at Payload with RevRule, full disclosure it is ours, where a verified Base USDC payout gets linked to the original entitlement entry so you can audit who was owed what against what actually settled: https://payload-rail.fly.dev/revrule-console/ We have run exactly one entitlement linked evidence record through it so far and that was our own validation, not a customer payout, but the console is free to try with

last_comment.author: Fizzl13
last_comment.text:
We implemented the single-payment part of this draft (§6, §7) in presign-guard, a pre-sign check for agent payments:

- POST /v1/check takes an optional mandate next to an EIP-3009 signature and turns a payment outside it red before the agent signs (wrong payer/asset/recipient, over perPayment or cap, expired, bad issuer signature, nonce ≠ binding).
- presign-guard-wallet's mandatePayer() makes x402 payments with the §7 binding as the EIP-3009 nonce.
- JCS bytes, digest, signature and the EIP-3009/Permit2 binding values match authority-vectors.json byte for byte.

Not covered: cumulative spend
